papers.title: The Birth of Plasmoids: Weibel-Driven Secondary Tearing and its Suppression in Relativistic Reconnection
papers.result: The authors find that plasmoids are initiated by a transverse electromagnetic current-filamentation/Weibel instability driven by extreme counter-streaming drift anisotropy ($z$-axis) near the primary x-line, rather than traditional Harris-sheet tearing. The dispersion relation in the cold limit yields a maximum growth rate $\Gamma_{\rm max} = \omega_p \beta_J \langle 1/\gamma \rangle^{1/2} \eta$ with $\beta_J^2 \equiv \langle \beta_z^2 / \gamma \rangle / \langle 1 / \gamma \rangle$ and measured growth $\Gamma_{\rm max} \sim 0.1\,\omega_{p0}$ peaking near upstream magnetization $\sigma_0 \sim 10$ (scaling as $\Gamma_{\rm max}/\omega_{p0} \propto \sigma_0^{1/2}$ in non-relativistic regimes). Plasma loading accumulates sheet surface density $\Sigma \sim n_0 \beta_{\rm rec} \ell (v_{A0}/v_{\rm out})$, reducing drift velocity $\beta_z \propto 1/\ell$ and effective anisotropy ratio $\frac{\Theta_z'}{\Theta_x'} \approx (1+\sigma_0)^2 \left( \frac{d_0}{\beta_{\rm rec}\ell} \right)^2$, completely quenching filamentation beyond the isotropization scale $\ell_{\rm iso} \sim \frac{1+\sigma_0}{\beta_{\rm rec}} d_0$ (or $\ell_{\rm iso} \sim 10\sigma_0 d_0$ for high $\sigma_0$ with reconnection rate $\beta_{\rm rec} \sim 0.1$).
papers.problem: The microphysical trigger and driver of secondary tearing and plasmoid birth in relativistic kinetic reconnection layers, as well as why and where secondary plasmoid generation is suppressed along the reconnection layer, have remained poorly understood.
papers.method: Two-dimensional relativistic PIC simulations using Tristan-MP v2 across $0.1 \le \sigma_0 \le 1000$ in anti-parallel pair plasma sheets, coupled with linear Vlasov-Maxwell stability analysis deriving the dispersion relation $c^2 k^2 (1 + M^2) = \omega_p^2 [\theta_x^{-1} W(\zeta) \langle \beta_z^2 / \gamma \rangle - \langle (1 - \beta_z^2) / \gamma \rangle]$ (where $\zeta = M / \sqrt{2\theta_x}$) and marginal stability marginalization for thermal quenching.
papers.reason: The paper provides a foundational kinetic breakthrough by uncovering that plasmoids in relativistic magnetic reconnection are born via Weibel-driven current filamentation induced by counter-streaming carrier anisotropy at the primary x-line, with the instability quenched at an isotropization scale $\ell_{\rm iso} \sim \frac{1+\sigma_0}{\beta_{\rm rec}} d_0$, governing plasmoid formation and reconnection morphology in relativistic jets and magnetar environments.

papers.title: Hidden Neutrino Active Galaxy Candidates: Prospects for Catalog and Stacking Searches with IceCube, IceCube-Gen2, and KM3NeT
papers.result: The combined all-flavor neutrino flux of the 28 candidates reaches $E_{\nu}^{2}\Phi_{\nu} \sim (1-3) \times 10^{-9}\ {\rm GeV\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}\ sr^{-1}}$, contributing $1-3\%$ of the diffuse flux measured at $\sim 10\ {\rm TeV}$. For individual detections over 10 years, NGC 1068 reaches up to $\sim 7\sigma$ in IceCube-Gen2 under Model A, while Circinus Galaxy reaches $\sim 6.7\sigma$ in KM3NeT under Model C based on $p_{j}=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{erfc}(\sqrt{q_{0,j}/2})$. Stacking searches excluding NGC 1068 can achieve a $5\sigma$ discovery within $\sim 5-10$ years for Models A and C.
papers.problem: Identifying promising obscured neutrino-emitting AGNs beyond NGC 1068 is hampered by uncertain coronal absorption corrections, large dispersions in SMBH mass estimates, and the lack of a standardized hard X-ray selected sample for stacking analyses.
papers.method: The authors synthesized the BASS, Swift/BAT 157-month, and NuSTAR surveys, applying torus obscuration models and an intrinsic hard X-ray flux cut $F_{X,\rm intr}^{2-195\ \rm keV} \ge 10^{-7}\ {\rm GeV\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$ to yield 28 candidates. Neutrino spectra were computed within the AMES framework for magnetically powered coronae across three representative turbulence and magnetic dissipation benchmarks (Models A, B, C), scaling parameters with Eddington ratio $\lambda_{\rm Edd} \equiv L_{\rm bol}/L_{\rm Edd}$ and coronal size $\mathcal{R} \equiv R_c / R_{\rm S}$.
papers.reason: The paper compiles the X-HiNAC sample of 28 jet-quiet AGNs to provide model-dependent high-energy neutrino predictions for IceCube-Gen2 and KM3NeT, directly connecting dense accretion coronas with multi-messenger searches.

papers.title: Intranight optical monitoring of eight quasars with superluminal jets and low optical polarization: Probing the mechanism of rapid flux variability
papers.result: For low-polarization superluminal quasars (LPSQs; $P_{\rm opt} < 3\%$ and apparent speeds $\beta_{\rm app}c = 5c - 31c$), the duty cycle (DC) of strong INOV (amplitude $\psi > 5\%$) is suppressed to $0\%$ under standard $F_\eta$ tests and only $\approx 7\%$ under the enhanced $F$-test, which is 3-10 times lower than in high-polarization quasars (HPQs, $\mathrm{DC} \sim 30\%$), demonstrating that high optical linear polarization rather than relativistic Doppler boosting is the primary driver and diagnostic of INOV.
papers.problem: Whether intranight optical variability in relativistic jets is primarily governed by bulk Doppler beaming (probed by high apparent superluminal speed $\beta_{\rm app}$) or by ordered magnetic field shocks (probed by high optical linear polarization $P_{\rm opt}$).
papers.method: Conducted 20 sessions of $R$-band monitoring ($\ge 3$ hr duration) using a 1.3-m telescope and combined them with 19 archival sessions for 8 LPSQs. Applied IRAF aperture photometry ($2\times\mathrm{FWHM}$), followed by the $F_\eta$ test (with scaling factor $\eta = 1.54$) and the enhanced $F$-test ($F_{\rm enh} = {\rm Var}(q-{\rm ref})/{\rm Var}_c$) to determine INOV status, amplitude $\psi = \sqrt{(A_{\max} - A_{\min})^2 - 2\sigma^2}$, and weighted duty cycle $\mathrm{DC}$.
papers.reason: The paper provides observational constraints on relativistic jet emission models by testing whether Doppler beaming or optical polarization primarily dictates intranight optical variability (INOV) in jetted active galactic nuclei.

papers.title: Probing the geometry and outflows of the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658 with multi-band polarimetry
papers.result: Optical linear polarisation is detected at $P = 0.3\text{--}1.5\%$ across $R$ and $I$ bands. During the main outburst, the weighted mean polarisation angles are $\overline{\Phi}_R = 34.6\pm 1.9^\circ$ and $\overline{\Phi}_I = 22.5\pm 1.7^\circ$, misaligned by $11.4^\circ\text{--}23.5^\circ$ from the X-ray spin axis determined by IXPE ($\mathrm{PA} = 46\pm 5^\circ$). In the subsequent reflare, $P_R$ peaks while $\Phi_R = 47.2\pm 3.4^\circ$ aligns with the IXPE axis, and $P$ correlates with color excess $(V-i')_{\rm jet}$ with weighted linear slopes of $0.84\pm 0.22$ ($R$) and $0.80\pm 0.13$ ($I$).
papers.problem: Distinguishing between disc atmosphere scattering, intrinsic non-thermal jet synchrotron emission, and magnetospheric boundary interactions as the primary driver of optical polarisation and its rapid geometric swings in accreting millisecond pulsars.
papers.method: Multi-band linear polarimetry using VLT/FORS2 in $R$ and $I$ filters combined with archival and concurrent IXPE 2–8 keV X-ray polarisation, alongside LCO multi-band optical monitoring to evaluate color-magnitude trajectories and jet Doppler boosting models with base tangential velocity $v_{\phi} \simeq 0.3c$ at $r \sim 20\text{--}30\text{ km}$.
papers.reason: This paper presents multi-epoch optical polarimetry of the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658 during its 2025 outburst, providing direct observational constraints on relativistic jet emission, Doppler boosting, and magnetospheric outflow geometry.

papers.title: The Valence and Inner Shell Ionization Properties of Sr I - III by Non-Thermal Electrons in Kilonovae
papers.result: Excitation-autoionization (EAI) constitutes roughly half of the total single ionization cross sections for $\mathrm{Sr\,I}$ and $\mathrm{Sr\,II}$, and omitting EAI leads to an error factor of up to $\sim 2$ in the derived ion abundances. Inner-shell ionization accounts for $30\% - 40\%$ of the total cross section in $\mathrm{Sr\,I}$ and $20\% - 30\%$ in $\mathrm{Sr\,II-III}$ at $5\,\mathrm{keV}$, scaling as $\propto \ln(E)/E$ at high energies; incorporating inner-shell ionization and Auger cascades modifies ion fractions by $20\% - 50\%$. Furthermore, approximately $20\% - 30\%$ of heavy atoms (e.g., Te) are ionized beyond triply ionized states at kilonova ejecta temperatures.
papers.problem: Standard kilonova spectral synthesis often relies on empirical Lotz cross sections ($\sigma_{\mathrm{Lotz}}(E) = \sum_i n_i a_i \frac{\ln(E/I_i)}{E I_i}$) that neglect excitation-autoionization (EAI) and inner-shell multi-electron ejection via Auger cascades, introducing significant systematic errors into non-thermal ionization balance and line identification.
papers.method: Level-resolved (J-split) and configuration-average (CA) electron impact cross sections were computed using the Flexible Atomic Code (FAC) with distorted wave and binary encounter dipole approximations up to $5\,\mathrm{keV}$. These cross sections were integrated into the `pynonthermal` Spencer-Fano solver under an energy deposition rate $q(t) = 0.15 \,(t / 1.4\,\mathrm{days})^{-1.3}\,\mathrm{eV\,s^{-1}\,ion^{-1}}$ to iteratively solve for the degraded electron spectrum $y(E)$ and the non-thermal steady-state ionization balance $\sum_{i \le j} \sum_{k > j-i} n_i \Gamma_{i,k} = n_{j+1} n_e \alpha_{j+1}(T)$.
papers.reason: This study accurately computes non-thermal electron impact ionization cross sections for Sr and investigates excitation-autoionization (EAI) and inner-shell Auger cascades, which directly impacts non-LTE ionization modeling of kilonova ejecta.

papers.title: CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS): Power Spectrum Injections and Survey Sensitivity
papers.result: For stacking depths of 1–30 days, CHAMPSS achieves maximum sensitivity for pulsar spin frequencies $f \approx 0.1\text{--}100\,\mathrm{Hz}$ and flux densities $S \gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{mJy}$. Monthly incoherent stacking increases the transmission fraction of faint sources ($0.1 < S < 1\,\mathrm{mJy}$) by up to $50\%$ (from $0.08\%$ in daily searches to $6.6\%$ in month-long searches). Both coherent and incoherent stacking scale in detection significance as $S_{\mathrm{min}} \propto N_{\mathrm{days}}^{-1/2}$, but red noise degrades the sensitivity at long periods ($P \gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{s}$, $f \lesssim 0.1\,\mathrm{Hz}$) by an order of magnitude compared to standard radiometer equation predictions.
papers.problem: Quantifying the search completeness and selection effects of all-sky pulsar stacking searches without computationally prohibitive and irreversible raw time-domain signal injections, while accounting for non-astrophysical red noise, scalloping loss, and Fast Dispersion Measure Transform (FDMT) covariance artifacts.
papers.method: Synthetic signal injection directly into Fourier power spectra across parameter grids of spin frequency $f \in [10^{-3}, 10^{2.7}]\,\mathrm{Hz}$, $\mathrm{DM}$, and flux density $S \in [0.001, 10]\,\mathrm{mJy}$. The pipeline incorporates normalized profile scaling $A = \frac{GS}{(T_{\mathrm{sys}}+T_{\mathrm{sky}})\beta}\sqrt{\frac{n_{\mathrm{days}}}{N_k}}\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{pol}}\Delta\nu\tau}$, effective temporal smearing $\Delta t_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx \sqrt{1.25\Delta t_{\mathrm{samp}}^2 + \Delta t_{\mathrm{dedisp}}^2 + \Delta t_{\mathrm{chan}}^2}$, sinc-squared scalloping attenuation $P_j = |a_j|^2 \mathrm{sinc}^2[\pi(r-j)]$, running median red noise normalization, and DBSCAN candidate clustering.
papers.reason: This paper presents the Fourier power spectrum injection framework and empirical sensitivity calibration for the CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS), characterizing pulse smearing, FDMT chromatic artifacts, and red noise limits relevant to blind pulsar and periodic transient searches.

papers.title: A Unified Mass-Loading Model for ASKAP J1745-5051: Linking Long-Period Radio Transients to Magnetic Cataclysmic Variables
papers.result: The high mass-loading branch reproduces the phased X-ray modulation with pulsed fractions of $28.00\%$ (0.3–1.5 keV) and $16.15\%$ (1.5–10 keV) through accretion curtain absorption and soft-cap beaming ($k_{\rm B}T_{\rm cap} \approx 0.14~{\rm keV}$, $k_{\rm B}T_{\rm sh} \approx 15~{\rm keV}$). The low mass-loading branch fed by donor stellar wind ($\dot{M}_{\rm w} = 10^{-14}~M_\odot~{\rm yr}^{-1}$) maintains a low density $n_{\rm e} \sim (1-4) \times 10^7~{\rm cm^{-3}}$, satisfying $\omega_{\rm p}/\omega_B \sim 0.03-0.06 \le 0.3$ and producing coherent ECME pulses at $\nu_{\rm obs} = 1~{\rm GHz}$ ($B \approx 373-392~{\rm G}$).
papers.problem: How coherent radio pulses characteristic of long-period transients (LPTs) can coexist with dense Roche-lobe overflow accretion and modulated X-ray emission at an identical $P_{\rm orb} \approx 82~{\rm min}$ period in ASKAP J1745-5051 without quenching the electron-cyclotron maser.
papers.method: Constructed a 3D binary magnetospheric model combining the magnetic fields $\boldsymbol{B}_{\rm tot} = \boldsymbol{B}_1 + \boldsymbol{B}_2$ of the white dwarf and donor star. Derived the mass-loading rate per unit flux $\Lambda = \rho_{\rm load} v_{\rm load} / B_{\rm load}$ where magnetic pressure $|\boldsymbol{B}_{\rm tot}|^2 / 4\pi \ge \xi \rho (v_\perp^2 + c_s^2)$, yielding parallel velocity profile $v_\parallel^2(\ell) = v_{\parallel,\rm load}^2 + 2 G M_1 [r(\ell)^{-1} - r_{\rm load}^{-1}]$ and density profile $n_{\rm e}(\ell) = \Lambda B(\ell) / [\mu_{\rm e} m_{\rm p} v_\parallel(\ell)]$ to evaluate hollow-cone ECME radio visibility and energy-dependent X-ray transfer.
papers.reason: This study develops a unified dual-branch mass-loading framework reconciling coherent electron-cyclotron maser emission (ECME) and magnetic accretion X-ray modulation in the long-period radio transient and cataclysmic variable ASKAP J1745-5051.

papers.title: Probing the nature of Galactic microquasars with diffuse gamma rays and neutrinos: low-mass versus high-mass X-ray binaries
papers.problem: Whether Galactic microquasars driving cosmic rays up to the PeV knee are dominated by low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs) or high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs), and how their distinct spatial distributions can be observationally discriminated using diffuse gamma rays and IceCube neutrinos.
papers.method: Cosmic-ray propagation is modeled via the spatially-dependent propagation (SDP) framework solved in DRAGON, combining background SNRs, a local young SNR (Geminga), and XRB sources parameterized with an injection spectrum $q_{\rm XB}(R) \propto (R/R_0)^{-\gamma_{\rm XB}} \exp(-R/R_c^{\rm XB})$ with $R_c^{\rm XB} = 5\ {\rm PV}$ and $\gamma_{\rm XB} = 2.1$, subsequently calculating $\pi^0$-decay diffuse gamma-ray and neutrino emissions.
papers.reason: This paper examines whether Galactic microquasars acting as cosmic-ray PeVatrons originate primarily from low-mass or high-mass X-ray binaries by modeling their spatial transport, diffuse gamma rays, and IceCube neutrino emissions. It directly informs research on relativistic jets, cosmic-ray PeVatrons, and multimessenger diffuse neutrino/gamma-ray signatures.

papers.title: A potential observational test to disentangle the companion of binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815
papers.result: For an ultra-massive $1.4\,M_\odot$ white dwarf companion, gravitational wave emission restricts the orbital period derivative to $\dot{P}_{\rm gw} = -(6.8-9.6)\times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ (or up to $-8.0\times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ for a $1.3\,M_\odot$ WD). For a $1.0-1.6\,M_\odot$ He star companion, evolutionary expansion yields $\dot{I}/I \approx (0.9-2.5)\times 10^{-8}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ and an extra tidal contribution $\dot{P}_{\rm tide} \approx -(0.4-1.0)\times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$, resulting in $\dot{P}_{\rm total} = \dot{P}_{\rm gw} + \dot{P}_{\rm tide} = -(4.9-13.5)\times 10^{-13}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ and setting an evaporation efficiency upper limit of $f_{\rm ev,max} \approx 0.006$.
papers.problem: Disentangling whether the companion of the eclipsing compact binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815 is an ultra-massive white dwarf or a stripped helium star, which cannot be decisively settled by current infrared photometric limits due to extinction and distance uncertainties.
papers.method: Combining the pulsar mass function $f(M_{\rm ns}, M_{\rm c}, i) = 0.2342\,M_\odot$ and eclipse-derived inclination $\sin i \approx 0.86-1.0$ with MESA stellar models to compute orbital angular momentum loss from both gravitational radiation $\dot{P}_{\rm gw}$ and tidal spin-orbit coupling $\dot{P}_{\rm tide} = -3rP(\dot{I}/I)$ with $r = J_{\rm s}/J_{\rm orb} \sim 0.003$.
papers.reason: The study provides an observational timing test to determine whether the companion of the eclipsing binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815 is an ultra-massive white dwarf or a stripped helium star via gravitational radiation and tidal coupling.

papers.title: Higher-Order Symmetry Energy Effects on the Properties of Neutron Stars
papers.result: Varying the symmetry energy curvature $K_{\mathrm{sym}}$ at fixed symmetry slope $L = 40\text{ MeV}$ has minimal impact on the maximum neutron star mass ($M_{\max} \sim 1.99\text{--}2.06\,M_\odot$ for TM1 and $1.89\text{--}1.93\,M_\odot$ for IUFSU), but strongly regulates the $1.4\,M_\odot$ stellar radius $R_{1.4}$ through identical linear scalings: $R_{1.4} = 13.3789 + 0.00961 K_{\mathrm{sym}}\,\mathrm{km}$ for TM1 ($R = 0.9999$) and $R_{1.4} = 11.5589 + 0.00957 K_{\mathrm{sym}}\,\mathrm{km}$ for IUFSU ($R = 0.9951$). Furthermore, larger $K_{\mathrm{sym}}$ leads to a reduced proton fraction $Y_p$ at suprasaturation density ($n_b \gtrsim 0.4\text{ fm}^{-3}$) via the chemical equilibrium relation $\mu_n - \mu_p \simeq 4 E_{\mathrm{sym}}(n_b)(1 - 2Y_p)$, shifting the direct Urca cooling threshold to higher densities.
papers.problem: Disentangling the specific impact of the poorly constrained higher-order symmetry energy curvature $K_{\mathrm{sym}}$ on neutron star equation of state, sound speed decomposition, proton fraction, direct Urca threshold, and stellar macroscopic properties independently of the lower-order parameters $J$ and $L$.
papers.method: Relativistic mean field (RMF) framework based on TM1 and IUFSU baselines, incorporating $\sigma, \delta, \omega, \rho$ mesons and leptons under $\beta$-equilibrium and charge neutrality ($\mu_n = \mu_p + \mu_e$, $\mu_e = \mu_\mu$, $n_p = n_e + n_\mu$), adjusting isovector couplings ($g_\rho, g_\delta, \Lambda_{\mathrm{V}}$) to systematically tune $K_{\mathrm{sym}}$ while fixing isoscalar saturation parameters and $L = 40\text{ MeV}$.
papers.reason: This paper establishes the exact quantitative sensitivity of neutron star radii and direct Urca cooling thresholds to the higher-order symmetry energy curvature $K_{\mathrm{sym}}$, providing a clean linear scaling relation $R_{1.4} \propto 0.0096 K_{\mathrm{sym}}$ useful for interpreting compact object equations of state and thermal evolution in high-energy transients.

papers.title: Symmetry energy effect on hot nuclear matter and proto-neutron stars
papers.result: Under isentropic conditions ($S = 0\text{--}3\,k_B$), increasing the entropy per baryon $S$ stiffens the EOS, supporting a larger PNS maximum mass $M_{\rm max}$ with lower central baryon density $n_b^c$ and higher central temperature $T_c$. For the TM1e parameter set ($L = 40\text{ MeV}$), the early trapped-neutrino phase ($S = 1, Y_L = 0.4$) yields $M_{\rm max} = 2.107\,M_\odot$ (slightly below the cold NS limit $2.121\,M_\odot$), and the smaller symmetry energy slope $L$ leads to higher core temperatures $T_c$ at identical $S$ and $Y_L$.
papers.problem: How the nuclear symmetry energy slope $L$ and thermal effects (isothermal temperature $T$ vs isentropic entropy $S$ and lepton fraction $Y_L$) modulate nuclear matter stiffness, proton fraction, and the mass-radius structure of hot proto-neutron stars during supernova core collapse.
papers.method: Relativistic mean field (RMF) model comparing TM1 ($L = 110.8\text{ MeV}$) and TM1e ($L = 40\text{ MeV}$) parameter sets, solving Fermi-Dirac nucleon distributions, chemical equilibrium under neutrino-trapped ($Y_L = 0.2, 0.4$) and neutrino-free ($Y_\nu = 0$) conditions, and computing the Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff structure with polytropic index $\gamma = \partial \ln P / \partial \ln \varepsilon$.
papers.reason: This work analyzes the impact of the nuclear symmetry energy slope $L$ and finite temperature/entropy on the equation of state and bulk properties of proto-neutron stars (PNSs), which directly governs the core-collapse supernova central engine and early remnant stability.

papers.title: Extreme Hard X-ray Variability in the TeV Blazar Mrk 421: Insights from NuSTAR Observations
papers.result: Mrk 421 exhibits extreme hard X-ray flux variability spanning a factor of 200–225 over 12 years (with an intra-day $P_{\rm var}$ up to $73\%$). The flux PDF favors a lognormal distribution (reduced $\chi^2 \sim 7$ versus $\sim 35$ for normal), accompanied by a linear RMS–flux relation ($r_s = 0.77$, $p = 4.38 \times 10^{-6}$). Spectra preferentially fit a log-parabolic model with photon index $\alpha \in [2.38, 3.64]$ and curvature $\beta \in [-0.33, 0.30]$, showing a strong 'harder-when-brighter' behavior where the synchrotron peak energy $E_{\rm p} = E_1 \times 10^{(2-\alpha)/(2\beta)}$ shifts from $\approx 0.23\,\mathrm{keV}$ to $\approx 3.57\,\mathrm{keV}$ and correlates tightly with flux ($r_{\mathrm{s}} = 0.82$). Scaling relations $\nu_{\mathrm{p}} \propto B \gamma_{\mathrm{p}}^2 \delta_{\mathrm{D}} / (1+z)$ and $F_\nu \propto K_{\mathrm{e}} B^{1+\alpha_{\mathrm{X}}} \delta_{\mathrm{D}}^{3+\alpha_{\mathrm{X}}}$ indicate variations are driven by magnetic field amplification and electron acceleration rather than Doppler factor Doppler boosting shifts alone.
papers.problem: Disentangling the driver of extreme X-ray variability and spectral curvature in TeV blazar relativistic jets: whether variations stem from additive stochastic processes or multiplicative cascading/turbulent processes, and whether peak shifts are governed by bulk Doppler beaming $\delta_{\mathrm{D}}$ or in situ electron acceleration and magnetic field fluctuations.
papers.method: Analyzed 27 NuSTAR observations (3–79 keV) from 2012 to 2024 using NuSTARDAS v1.3.1 and HEASOFT v6.33 with standard source ($30''$) and background ($60''$) apertures. Performed timing analysis via excess variance $\sigma^2_{\rm XS}$, fractional variability $F_{\rm var}$, and non-Gaussian variability amplitude $P_{\rm var} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}} \frac{1}{x_{\rm med}} \sqrt{\sum_{i} (x_i - x_{\rm med})^2 \cdot \frac{\delta_{\rm med}^2}{\delta_i^2}}$. Tested normal vs lognormal flux PDFs and modeled 3–79 keV spectra using power-law (PL), broken power-law (BPL), and log-parabolic (LP) models ($F(E) = K (E/E_0)^{-\alpha - \beta \log(E/E_0)}$) fixed at Galactic $N_{\rm H} = 1.34 \times 10^{20}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$.
papers.reason: The paper provides an extensive 12-year NuSTAR timing and spectral analysis (3–79 keV across 27 epochs) of the TeV blazar Mrk 421, delivering concrete scaling relations for synchrotron peak shifts and flux distributions relevant to relativistic jet dynamics and particle acceleration.

papers.title: Deconvolved IXPE Polarization Maps of the Crab Nebula in a Maximum-a-Posteriori Framework
papers.result: Deconvolution of IXPE 2–8 keV observations yields a sharper spatial structure around the Crab jet with best-fit hyperparameters $\boldsymbol{\mu}^{\ast} = (1.82\times 10^{-6}, 5.04\times 10^{-8}, 1.68\times 10^{-8})$. In jet subregion $\mathcal{S}$, the magnetic-field orientation is nearly perpendicular to the intensity gradient with a weighted mean resultant length $\bar{R}_{w} = 0.61$, statistically significant at $p = 0.0012$ against unpolarized null models.
papers.problem: IXPE observations of the Crab Nebula are degraded by the telescope point spread function (half-power diameter $\sim 25''$) and detector electron-track scattering, which limits spatial resolution of magnetic field structures in the jet and inner nebula.
papers.method: Formulated polarization-map reconstruction as an inverse problem in discretized 3D sky-polarization space ($N_x \times N_y \times N_q = 35 \times 35 \times 16$), maximizing joint posterior $(I^{\ast},f^{\ast})=\operatorname{argmax}_{I\ge 0, f\ge 0}[\log p(Y\mid I,f) - \mu_{1}V_{1}(I) - \mu_{2}V_{2}(I) - \mu_{3}V_{3}(f)]$ via L-BFGS-B optimization, with hyperparameters tuned by 5-fold cross-validation and Bayesian optimization.
papers.reason: The paper develops a maximum-a-posteriori (MAP) deconvolution framework to deconvolve IXPE spatial and polarization data of the Crab Nebula, revealing jet magnetic field geometries and resolving instrumental PSF and track scattering.

papers.title: Angular Momentum Transport across Accretion States around a rapidly spinning black hole
papers.result: In the MAD state, the total angular momentum flux is radially conserved ($\propto r^{-0.01}$), with $96\%$–$105\%$ carried outward by the coherent Blandford–Znajek jet channel ($\propto r^{-0.08}$) dominated by laminar Maxwell stress $-\langle b^r\rangle\langle b_\varphi\rangle$. The effective viscous stress parameter scales as $\alpha_{\rm visc} \propto r^{-0.30}$ in MAD, $r^{-0.56}$ in INT, and $r^{-0.35}$ in SANE, resulting in a viscous timescale $t_{\rm visc}/t_{\rm dyn} \approx 84$–$93$ at $10$–$40\,r_g$ in MAD (accelerating disk evolution by a factor of $\sim 3.5$–$4.5$ relative to SANE). During flux eruptions triggered by magnetic interchange instability, the horizon magnetic flux $\phi_{r_H}$ drops by up to $52.0\%$ (from $53.95$ to $25.87$) and mass accretion rate $|\dot{M}|_{r_H}$ drops by $40.6\%$, accompanied by a net sign reversal of angular momentum flux across the jet boundary at $10\,r_g$ (from $+2.19$ to $-0.90$), a doubling of jet tilt angle $\theta_{\rm tilt}$ from $9.21^\circ$ to $21.87^\circ$, and funnel narrowing ($\theta_{\rm open}$ contracting by $5\%$ to $62.85^\circ$).
papers.problem: How magnetic flux accumulation transitions the physical mechanism of angular momentum transport—from MRI-driven turbulent stresses to large-scale laminar magnetic torques—and how episodic magnetic flux eruption events dynamically alter relativistic jet launching, boundary flux exchange, and jet orientation around an extreme Kerr black hole ($a=0.998$).
papers.method: Three-dimensional GRMHD simulations using the H-AMR code in Kerr-Schild coordinates ($N_r \times N_\theta \times N_\phi = 448 \times 240 \times 192$) initialized with a Fishbone-Moncrief torus ($\tilde{\Gamma} = 13/9$, $\beta=100$). Flow regions are identified via magnetization $\sigma = b^2/\rho > 1$ (jet) and radial velocity criteria (wind vs. disk). Angular momentum flux $\dot{\mathcal{J}}^r$ is decomposed via Reynolds averaging into advective $\dot{\mathcal{J}}^r_{\rm adv}$ and stress terms $\dot{\mathcal{J}}^r_{\rm stress} = \dot{\mathcal{J}}^r_{\rm Max,lam} + \dot{\mathcal{J}}^r_{\rm Max,turb} + \dot{\mathcal{J}}^r_{\rm Rey}$, and magnetic eruption events are tracked via horizon flux dips $\Delta\phi_{r_H}$ alongside equatorial current sheet diagnostics.
papers.reason: This study presents high-resolution 3D GRMHD simulations of accretion flows around an extreme Kerr black hole ($a=0.998$), offering quantitative scalings of angular momentum transport, jet collimation, and flux eruption dynamics essential for modeling relativistic jet engines and compact object flares.

papers.title: Effects of Competing Reactions on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ on Abundance Distributions in Type I X-Ray Bursts
papers.result: Secondary abundance peaks for 44 nuclides arise when the $(p,\alpha)/(p,\gamma)$ reaction rate ratios for $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ reach $\sim 1.0\times 10^4$ and $4.2\times 10^3$ times their median ratios, respectively. Fixing both reaction pairs to their STARLIB median rates reduces the secondary-peak fraction by $96\%$--$100\%$ across all 44 nuclides and drops the number of isotopes with regression $\mathrm{RMSE} > 0.2\,\mathrm{dex}$ from 95 to 23.
papers.problem: Nuclear reaction-rate uncertainties in the $rp$-process cause non-Gaussian bimodal abundance distributions (secondary peaks) in Type I X-ray burst ashes, whose underlying reaction drivers and physical mechanisms were not systematically understood.
papers.method: One-zone post-processing nucleosynthesis calculation along the K04 trajectory ($T_{\rm peak} = 1.36\,\mathrm{GK}$, $\rho \sim 0.54$--$1.44 \times 10^6\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$, duration $\sim 100\,\mathrm{s}$) using the WinNet network (686 nuclides) with log-normal Monte Carlo sampling ($r_{ij} = r_{\mathrm{med}}(\mathrm{f.u.})^{p_{ij}}$, $p_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,1)$, $10^5$ runs) coupled to XGBoost classification and TreeSHAP feature importance analysis.
papers.reason: The paper identifies the nuclear reaction pairs $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}(p,\alpha)/(p,\gamma)$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}(p,\alpha)/(p,\gamma)$ as the dominant cause of bimodal secondary abundance peaks in Type I X-ray burst nucleosynthesis using Monte Carlo simulations combined with XGBoost and SHAP analysis.

papers.title: Angle-dependent emission from evolving accretion layers
papers.result: Time-dependent expansion and heating fundamentally alter the emergent angular contrast $C = I_s(0.1)/I_s(1)$. As dimensionless heating increases from $\mathcal{H}=0$ to $\mathcal{H}=4$, the emergent radiation transitions from limb darkening ($C = 0.436$) to limb brightening ($C = 1.264$). In comparison to stationary frozen-source benchmarks, the relative correction $(C_{\rm TD}/C_{\rm FS})-1 = (e_{0.1}-e_1)/(1+e_1)$ changes sign from $+31\%$ in optically thin, fast-expanding layers ($\tau_0 \sim 0.12$) to $-5.9\%$ in thicker layers ($\tau_0 \sim 0.9$), driven by oblique photon flight paths sampling non-negligible flow age fractions $(t-t_b)/t = (\eta_s-\eta_b)/(\mu-\eta_b)$.
papers.problem: Whether time-dependent propagation effects in dynamic, expanding accretion flows (such as super-Eddington winds and tidal disruption events) break stationary radiative transfer assumptions and modify emergent angular intensity profiles when photon flight times are comparable to the expansion timescale.
papers.method: A 1D plane-parallel, grey, special-relativistic self-similar radiation hydrodynamics formulation in similarity coordinate $\eta = z/(ct)$, with density $\rho_0 = R(\eta)/(\chi ct)$ and radiative intensity $I = \frac{c^2}{4\pi\chi t} i(\eta,\mu)$. The conservative transport equation $\frac{\partial}{\partial\eta}[(\mu-\eta)i] = R(D^3 s_0 - D^{-1}i)$ (where Doppler factor $D = [\gamma(1-\beta\mu)]^{-1}$) is coupled directly to mass continuity $C_m = \gamma R(\beta-\eta)$ and radiative acceleration $\gamma^3 (\beta-\eta)\beta' = h_0$ without ad-hoc Eddington closures, solved via an upwind finite-volume scheme and Gauss-Legendre angular quadrature.
papers.reason: The paper develops a 1D self-similar, special-relativistic, grey radiative transfer hydrodynamic model for expanding accretion layers, demonstrating that non-stationary evolution alters the emergent angular intensity contrast $C = I(0.1)/I(1)$ by up to tens of percent.

papers.title: A Massive and Eccentric Binary Millisecond Pulsar in the Globular Cluster M10
papers.result: Timing of PSR J1657$-$0406A shows $P = 4.7340689751208(4)\text{ ms}$, ${\rm DM} = 43.885(4)\text{ pc cm}^{-3}$, orbital period $P_{\rm b} = 37.3986270(14)\text{ days}$, and eccentricity $e = 0.1192287(4)$. The mass function is $f_{\rm M} = 0.0022196651(14)\ {\rm M}_\odot$, and periastron advance is $\dot{\omega} = 0.00090(13)\text{ deg yr}^{-1}$, yielding total system mass $M_{\rm tot} = 2.5(6)\ {\rm M}_\odot$, pulsar mass $M_{\rm p} = 2.2^{+0.6}_{-0.5}\ {\rm M}_\odot$, and companion mass $M_{\rm c} = 0.26^{+0.17}_{-0.03}\ {\rm M}_\odot$.
papers.problem: Investigating whether the significant eccentricity ($e \sim 0.12$) in this wide millisecond pulsar binary originated from dynamical secondary exchange encounters, passing-star gravitational perturbations, or intrinsic binary evolution.
papers.method: Phase-coherent pulse timing spanning nearly seven years of FAST 1.0–1.5 GHz observations with PRESTO, TEMPO, and DRACULA using the DD binary model, combined with FEWBODY dynamical scatterings and HST non-detection photometric limits.
papers.reason: FAST timing of the binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1657$-$0406A in globular cluster M10 reveals a massive neutron star in an eccentric orbit, shedding light on dense cluster dynamical perturbations and pulsar mass constraints.

papers.title: A magnetically heated slim disc-corona model for tidal disruption events
papers.result: The model successfully accounts for the spectral and temporal evolution of TDE AT2021ehb, deriving a black hole mass $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=6.317\pm 0.055$. The accretion rate follows a power-law decay $\dot{m}_{\rm XRT}=0.44(t/120\,{\rm d})^{-1.60}$, while rapid hardening is driven by a $\sim 300$-fold drop in the plasma parameter $\beta=(p_{\rm gas}+p_{\rm rad})/p_{\rm B}$. A lower limit for Comptonized photon index $\Gamma \sim 2$ is established due to disk reprocessing seed photons.
papers.problem: Standard thin disc-corona and slim disc models suffer from unphysical discontinuities across radiation- and gas-pressure dominated regimes, and fail to self-consistently explain the rapid X-ray brightening, state transitions, and hard coronal emission observed in TDEs like AT2021ehb.
papers.method: A unified set of slim disc equations is solved simultaneously incorporating gas pressure $p_{\rm gas}$, radiation pressure $p_{\rm rad}$, magnetic pressure $p_{\rm B}$, advection cooling $Q_{\rm adv}^- = \frac{\dot{M}}{4\pi R^2}\frac{p}{\rho_{\rm d}}\xi$, and coronal dissipation $Q_{\rm cor}^- = \frac{B^2}{4\pi}V_{\rm A}$, coupled to vertical hydrostatic equilibrium $p/\rho_{\rm d}=\Omega_{\rm K}^2 H^2$ and local energy conservation $(Q_{\rm vis}^+-Q_{\rm adv}^-)(1-f_{\rm c})=Q_{\rm rad}^-$. Hard X-ray Comptonization spectra are evaluated via Monte Carlo simulations.
papers.reason: The paper develops a self-consistent magnetically heated slim disc-corona model across near- to super-Eddington regimes, providing physical scalings and spectral tables to interpret TDE X-ray spectral transitions.

papers.title: Signatures of quark matter from neutron star mass-radius curve
papers.result: The study demonstrates that the turnover mass where $\mathrm{d}R/\mathrm{d}M = 0$ peaks at median values $M_{\rm turn} = 1.258\,M_\odot$ for nucleonic stars, $1.521\,M_\odot$ for hyperonic stars, and $1.691\,M_\odot$ for hybrid stars, establishing $M_{\rm turn} > 1.7\,M_\odot$ as strong evidence for quark matter. Furthermore, defining the differential curvature quantity $X = [R(2.0\,M_\odot) - R(1.6\,M_\odot)] - [R(1.6\,M_\odot) - R(1.4\,M_\odot)]$, values of $X > -0.2\,\mathrm{km}$ serve as a clean indicator for hybrid stars, while nucleonic models yield $X < -0.24\,\mathrm{km}$.
papers.problem: Identifying distinguishing phenomenological signatures of internal degrees of freedom (nucleons, hyperons, and deconfined quarks) directly from neutron star mass-radius ($M$-$R$) observations subject to multi-messenger and nuclear physics constraints.
papers.method: Statistical analysis of over 250,000 relativistic mean field (RMF) equations of state combined with NJL and MFTQCD models constrained by chiral effective field theory ($\chi\mathrm{EFT}$), perturbative QCD (pQCD) boundary conditions, NICER, and GW170817, validated against the CompOSE database.
papers.reason: The paper provides concrete phenomenological metrics ($M_{\rm turn} > 1.7\,M_\odot$ and $X > -0.2\,\mathrm{km}$) to identify deconfined quark matter in neutron star cores from mass-radius ($M$-$R$) curves, directly connecting dense matter EOS to compact object high-energy astrophysical observations.

papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Signal from a Short GRB Relativistic MHD Jet
papers.result: The sGRB relativistic jet generates a memory-type gravitational-wave signal with low-frequency strain amplitude $|\tilde{h}(f)| \propto 1/f$ and a characteristic knee at $f \sim 0.3\text{--}0.5\,\mathrm{Hz}$ set by the injection duration $t_{\rm inj} = 2\,\mathrm{s}$. At $D = 10\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, the strain plateau reaches $h_{+} \simeq 2.5 \times 10^{-24}$ for $\theta_v = 30^{\circ}\text{--}40^{\circ}$, accompanied by an early negative dip at $t' \approx 0.044\,\mathrm{s}$ caused by lateral equatorial momentum exchange from Poynting flux.
papers.problem: Standard gravitational-wave quadrupole approximations fail for ultra-relativistic collimated outflows, making it necessary to develop numerical retarded integration to evaluate GW waveforms, memory features, and detectability from sGRB MHD jets.
papers.method: Direct volume integration of retarded linearized Einstein equations in the wave zone without quadrupole approximations, splitting $T_{ij} = T_{ij}^{(\mathrm{matter})} + T_{ij}^{(\mathrm{EM})}$ into kinetic, electric, and magnetic contributions, post-processing 2D axisymmetric relativistic MHD simulations of a Poynting-dominated jet with luminosity $L = 4\times 10^{50}\,\mathrm{erg/s}$ expanding into merger ejecta.
papers.reason: This work explores gravitational-wave memory signals produced by relativistic MHD jets from short GRBs, offering concrete waveforms and spectral signatures relevant to compact object central engines.

papers.title: Self-lensing of electromagnetic counterparts to extreme mass ratio inspirals
papers.result: Self-lensing by the central SMBH generates alternating flare magnifications and asymmetric 'trailing shoulder' light curve profiles due to Keplerian orbital motion. The recurrence of lensing envelope maxima matches the nodal Lense-Thirring precession period ($T_{\mathrm{LT}}^{\mathrm{infer}} = 2 T_{\mathrm{env}} = 8.231 \times 10^5\,M$ versus theoretical $T_{\mathrm{LT}}^{\mathrm{th}} = 8.278 \times 10^5\,M$). At $r_s = 50\,M$ and threshold $\mu_{\mathrm{th}} = 1.2$, the single-flare lensing probability is $P_{1.2} \simeq 3.1\%$, while nodal precession increases cumulative probability to $P_{1.2}^{(\mathrm{c})} \simeq 34.8\%$, following the radial scalings $P_{1.2}(r_s) \simeq 3.1\% (r_s / 50\,M)^{-1}$ and $P_{1.2}^{(\mathrm{c})} \simeq 34.8\% (r_s / 50\,M)^{-1/2}$.
papers.problem: How strong gravitational self-lensing by a spinning supermassive black hole modulates the light curves, shapes, and spectral evolution of disk-crossing flares from inclined EMRI systems, and whether self-lensing can explain alternating amplitudes and multi-peaked substructures in quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs).
papers.method: Forward ray tracing in Kerr spacetime integrating null geodesics using Carter constants $(\lambda, q)$ for direct ($N=0$) and lensed ($N=1$) images, mapped to Boyer-Lindquist disk-crossing positions $x_{s,i}^\mu = (t_i, r_{s,i}, \pi/2, \phi_{s,i})$ with both static ($\Omega_{s,i}=0$) and Keplerian ($\Omega_{s,i} = \Omega_{\mathrm{K}}(r_{s,i}) = (r_{s,i}^{3/2} + a)^{-1}$) hotspot kinematics, convolved with a fast-rise exponential-decay intrinsic flare luminosity profile $L_{\mathrm{int},i}(\tilde{t})$.
papers.reason: The paper investigates general-relativistic self-lensing of repeating electromagnetic flares from inclined EMRIs crossing accretion disks around a Kerr SMBH, offering direct diagnostic signatures for QPE profiles and timing.

papers.title: Hidden by Exponential Screening: The Invisibility of the Dymnikova Black Hole de Sitter Core to Accretion Observables
papers.result: Due to the exponential screening factor $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2 M)}$, corrections to the metric decay rapidly outside the horizon. Even for near-extremal critical scales $l_{\rm cr} = 1.1M$ where gravitational acceleration deviates by $\delta g/g_{\rm S} \approx 12\%$ at $r = 2.3M$, the hydrodynamic impact is strictly confined to $r \lesssim 2.7M$. Across all models, time-averaged accretion rates differ from Schwarzschild by $|\Delta \langle \dot{M} \rangle| / \langle \dot{M} \rangle < 0.8\%$ ($2\sigma$), the shock-cone opening angle remains $1.077 \pm 0.003\ \mathrm{rad}$, the stagnation radius is $r_{\rm st} = 26.8 \pm 0.3M$, and inward fluctuation propagation lags ($\tau_{12 \to 6.11} = 75.5 \pm 1.0M$ and $\tau_{6.11 \to 2.3} = 31.6 \pm 0.4M$) agree within $1.6\%$, rendering the de Sitter core undetectable via accretion timing.
papers.problem: Whether the de Sitter regular core replacing the central singularity in Dymnikova black holes can produce detectable signatures in relativistic Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion flow observables (such as mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$, shock-cone geometry, QPOs, and time lags) in high-energy compact objects.
papers.method: 2D equatorial general relativistic hydrodynamics (GRHD) simulations of Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion onto fixed Dymnikova backgrounds ($0.1M \le l_{\rm cr} \le 1.1M$, up to $97\%$ of extremal limit $l_{\rm cr}^{\rm ext} = 1.1379M$) with lapse $f(r) = 1 - 2M(1 - e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2 M)})/r$, combined with Whittle-likelihood power spectrum analysis, ensemble averaging, and cross-spectral time lag diagnostics $\tau_{a\to b}(f) = \arg[G_{ab}(f)]/(2\pi f)$.
papers.reason: Investigates whether Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion observables (timing lags, QPOs, accretion rate) can constrain regular black holes with a de Sitter core, establishing an observational degeneracy limit with standard Schwarzschild black holes for high-energy compact object timing studies.

papers.title: Two Fast Radio Burst Candidates Detected in the RATAN-600 Blind Survey
papers.result: Two FRB candidates were detected at 4.7 GHz with dispersion measures $\mathrm{DM} = 200\pm 20\ \mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ ($z \approx 0.09$, $E_{\mathrm{iso}} \sim 10^{40}\ \mathrm{erg}$) and $\mathrm{DM} = 266\pm 10\ \mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ ($z \approx 0.13$, $E_{\mathrm{iso}} \approx 2\times 10^{40}\ \mathrm{erg}$). The inferred sky rate is $\sim 27.5\ \mathrm{events\ yr^{-1}\ sky^{-1}}$ at $\sim 1\ \mathrm{Jy}$, which is roughly two orders of magnitude below the ASKAP CRAFT rate scaled from 1.4 GHz.
papers.problem: Investigating the occurrence rate, spectral bandwidth, and propagation properties of FRBs at high radio frequencies (4.4–5.0 GHz), which show a large rate discrepancy compared to low-frequency surveys.
papers.method: Multi-channel Gaussian pulse modeling accounting for intra-channel dispersion smearing and delay $\Delta t \propto \nu_1^{-2} - \nu_2^{-2}$, fitted via Bayesian nested sampling (UltraNest/MLFriends) along with an 8th-order Butterworth low-pass filter.
papers.reason: Reports the detection of two high-frequency (4.4-5.0 GHz) FRB candidates in the RATAN-600 blind survey and places empirical constraints on the high-frequency event rate.

papers.title: X-ray Variability of Mrk 421 in 2025 January: A Ten-Day XPoSat XSPECT Campaign with Contemporaneous NICER Coverage
papers.result: The blazar exhibited strong X-ray variability with fractional variability $F_{\rm var} = 19.6\pm 0.3\%$ over 10 days, resolving 26 Bayesian block states spanning a factor of 2.34 in flux. The flare profile revealed asymmetric morphology with rise time $\tau_r = 0.124\pm 0.020\ {\rm d}$ and decay time $\tau_d = 1.23\pm 0.39\ {\rm d}$ (asymmetry $\zeta=0.82$), contrasting with shorter synchrotron cooling timescales ($t_{\rm cool,obs}\sim 15\ {\rm min}$ to $9\ {\rm h}$). Spectra follow a log-parabola model demonstrating harder-when-brighter behavior, with 1 keV photon index $\alpha$ hardening from $\approx 2.24$ to $\approx 1.96$ and synchrotron peak shifting from $\approx 0.66\ {\rm keV}$ to $1.06\ {\rm keV}$, while identical count rates exhibit distinct photon indices ($\Delta\Gamma = 0.26$, $6.4\sigma$ difference) between flare rise and decay phases.
papers.problem: Investigating the acceleration and cooling dynamics of emitting electrons in blazar relativistic jets, testing whether instantaneous count rate uniquely determines the X-ray spectral state, and constraining flux distributions and PSD slopes.
papers.method: Analysis of 202 ks XPoSat/XSPECT (0.8–15 keV) observations combined with contemporaneous NICER (0.3–10 keV) data using Bayesian block segmentation, Whittle and PSRESP-based power spectral density fitting ($P(\nu)=A\nu^{-s}+c$), sum-of-exponentials (SOE) flare profile modeling, and absorption-corrected log-parabola spectral fitting ($\mathrm{TBabs}\times\mathrm{logpar}$).
papers.reason: The paper presents multi-day timing and spectral analysis of the blazar Mrk 421 using XPoSat/XSPECT and NICER, constraining particle acceleration and cooling timescales in relativistic blazar jets.

papers.title: Decomposition of disk and jet optical emission: Case of PKS~1510-089 and PKS~0736+017
papers.result: Decomposition reveals an accretion disk continuum fraction of $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.37^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$ (mean jet polarization $\bar{p}_{\mathrm{j}} = 3.60^{+0.03}_{-0.03}\%$, $\tau_{\mathrm{H}\beta} = 54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}\,\mathrm{days}$) for PKS 1510-089, and $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$ ($\bar{p}_{\mathrm{j}} = 2.05^{+0.03}_{-0.02}\%$, $\tau_{\mathrm{H}\beta} = 84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}\,\mathrm{days}$) for PKS 0736+017, moving corrected disk luminosities closer to the canonical $R_{\mathrm{BLR}}-L_{5100}$ relation.
papers.problem: In flat-spectrum radio quasars, intense Doppler-boosted non-thermal synchrotron emission from relativistic jets heavily contaminates optical continuum emission, decoupling continuum from broad emission line variability and distorting the canonical $R_{\mathrm{BLR}}-L_{5100}$ relationship and black hole mass estimates.
papers.method: Bayesian light-curve decomposition framework (DECOMP) modeling disk $C_d(t)$ and jet $C_j(t)$ as independent Damped Random Walk (DRW) processes with covariance $S_{\star}(\Delta t) = \sigma_{\star}^{2}\exp(-|\Delta t|/T_{\star})$, convolving with Gaussian transfer functions $\Psi(\tau) = \frac{f_{\star}}{\sqrt{2\pi\omega_{\star}^2}}\exp\left[-\frac{(\tau-\tau_{\star})^2}{2\omega_{\star}^2}\right]$ for $\mathrm{H}\beta$ and 37 GHz radio curves, coupled with Stokes parameters ($I, Q, U$) and polarization constraints.
papers.reason: The paper provides an observational decomposition of non-thermal relativistic jet synchrotron emission and thermal accretion disk continuum in two gamma-ray bright FSRQs (PKS 1510-089 and PKS 0736+017) using polarimetry and reverberation mapping, directly relevant to relativistic jet contamination and BLR scaling relations.

papers.title: A Multi-messenger Study of the Cygnus bubble
papers.result: Joint Bayesian fitting of $\gamma$-ray spectra and spatial profiles reveals that Bohm diffusion is the only viable regime explaining emission up to sub-PeV energies, yielding reduced $\chi^2_{\rm red} \approx 1.57$, whereas Kolmogorov ($\chi^2_{\rm red} = 31.88$) and Kraichnan ($\chi^2_{\rm red} = 10.09$, requiring unrealistic $\mathcal{L}_{\rm sw} = 2.83\times 10^{39}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$ and $\eta_B = 10\%$) are strongly disfavored. Ionised gas dominates the $\gamma$-ray output. The predicted neutrino fluxes yield expected detection significances in Bohm diffusion after 1, 5, and 10 years of exposure of $1.30\sigma$, $2.91\sigma$, and $4.11\sigma$ for IceCube, and $1.01\sigma$, $2.25\sigma$, and $3.18\sigma$ for KM3NeT/ARCA.
papers.problem: Whether stellar wind termination shocks in young massive star clusters like Cyg OB2 can accelerate protons up to the cosmic-ray knee ($E_p \sim 3\ {\rm PeV}$), what diffusion regime governs particle confinement and escape, and whether the observed extended ultra-high-energy $\gamma$-ray and neutrino emissions can be self-consistently reconciled with target gas morphologies.
papers.method: A 1D steady-state spherical cosmic-ray transport model is adopted with diffusive shock acceleration at the termination shock $\mathcal{R}_{\rm sh}$, with terminal shock proton spectrum $N_{\rm sh}(p) \propto (p/m_p c)^{-s} e^{-\Gamma(p)}$ and turbulent magnetic field $\delta \mathcal{B}_{\rm sw} = [\eta_B \dot{M}_\star u_{\rm sw} / (2r^2)]^{1/2}$. Gas densities (molecular, atomic, ionized) are reconstructed from radio/IR surveys (CGPS, PMO, Planck). Bayesian parameter estimation is performed with Nautilus by evaluating a joint log-likelihood against SED data (Fermi-LAT, HAWC, ARGO, LHAASO) and LHAASO surface brightness profiles.
papers.reason: The paper provides a detailed multi-messenger investigation of the Cygnus bubble PeVatron using joint SED and surface brightness modeling, constraining cosmic-ray diffusion modes and predicting neutrino event rates for IceCube and KM3NeT.

papers.title: A GeV PWN Candidate in the PSR J1135--6055/G293.8+0.6 Field
papers.result: A point-source gamma-ray excess is detected above $20\ \mathrm{GeV}$ up to $1\ \mathrm{TeV}$ with $\mathrm{TS}=26.30$, best-fit coordinates $(\alpha, \delta) = (173.733^{\circ}, -60.910^{\circ})$, and a hard photon index $\Gamma = 1.63 \pm 0.33$, consistent with the position of PSR J1135-6055 within $r_{95} \simeq 3'$.
papers.problem: Investigating whether a high-energy GeV gamma-ray counterpart exists associated with the pulsar wind nebula and jet structure of PSR J1135-6055 inside the composite SNR G293.8+0.6.
papers.method: Maximum-likelihood morphological and spectral analysis of nearly 18 years of Fermi-LAT data ($20\ \mathrm{GeV} - 1\ \mathrm{TeV}$) using a power-law point source model with low-frequency timing noise modeled via PINT using $F_0-F_2$ and harmonic WAVEX terms.
papers.reason: The paper reports a newly detected GeV gamma-ray counterpart spatially coincident with the pulsar wind nebula (PWN) of PSR J1135-6055 in SNR G293.8+0.6, providing direct high-energy constraints on the compact object engine and relativistic lepton population.

papers.title: Stellar wind variability in OB stars and its effect on mass-loss determinations
papers.result: The co-rotating interaction region (CIR) framework produces spiral structures characterized by density enhancements of $\sim 2$ and velocity plateaus that boost the Sobolev optical depth $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}$ by factors of $10$ to $100$, resolving why mass-loss determinations neglecting clumping and large-scale wind structures differ by factors of $\gtrsim 10$.
papers.problem: Empirical mass-loss rates ($\dot{M}$) inferred across UV, optical, infrared, and radio diagnostics exhibit discrepancies by factors of $10$ or more due to wind variability, discrete absorption components (DACs), and non-spherical clumping.
papers.method: Hydrodynamic CIR modeling and the Sobolev with extra integration (SEI) radial optical depth formulation $\tau_{\mathrm{rad}}(w) \propto \frac{\dot{M}}{R_\star v_\infty^2} \frac{q_i(w)}{x^2 w} \left(\frac{\mathrm{d}w}{\mathrm{d}x}\right)^{-1}$ combined with mm/radio free-free bremsstrahlung continuum flux (scaling as $\propto \rho^2$ and sensitive to clumping factor $f_{\mathrm{cl}} = \langle \rho^2 \rangle / \langle \rho \rangle^2$).
papers.reason: Accurate determination of OB-star mass-loss rates and wind structure provides crucial benchmark conditions for core-collapse supernova progenitors and their circumstellar environments.

papers.title: Milliarcsecond-scale jet reorientations in GRS 1915+105 pointing towards a warped accretion disc
papers.result: VLBI observations across 4 epochs between 2019 and 2021 reveal a maximum jet position angle (PA) offset of $57^{\circ}\pm 8^{\circ}$ from the historical pre-obscured axis ($142^{\circ}\pm 7^{\circ}$). In epoch EVN E1, a rapid flare is observed with flux rising by $>150\,\mathrm{mJy}$ in 3 hours and brightness temperature lower limits of $T_b \approx 6\times 10^6 - 7\times 10^8\,\mathrm{K}$. Across 126 days between EVN E1 ($\mathrm{PA}=18.6^{\circ}$) and EVN E2 ($\mathrm{PA}=170.9^{\circ}$), the minimum angular displacement is $27.7^{\circ}$, giving a sky-projected slew rate $\dot{\rm PA}\gtrsim 0.2^{\circ}\,{\rm d}^{-1}$. The approaching-to-receding component separation ratio $\frac{\Delta r_{\rm a}}{\Delta r_{\rm r}}=\frac{1+\beta\cos{i}}{1-\beta\cos{i}}$ yields $1.28\pm 0.06$ and $1.25\pm 0.02$, favoring an inclination $i \sim 64^{\circ}\pm 4^{\circ}$ over edge-on geometry ($i\sim 87^{\circ}-89^{\circ}$) for $\beta \sim 0.35$.
papers.problem: Investigating whether the severe X-ray obscuration and drastic radio jet position angle variations observed in GRS 1915+105 originate from rapid inner-disc Lense-Thirring precession or outer-disc radiative warping instabilities.
papers.method: Multi-epoch milliarcsecond-scale VLBI observations using VLBA (8.4 GHz) and EVN (4.9 GHz) calibrated via AIPS and Difmap, combined with kinematic modeling of relativistic ejection pairs using the separation ratio $\frac{\Delta r_{\mathrm{a}}}{\Delta r_{\mathrm{r}}}=\frac{1+\beta\cos{i}}{1-\beta\cos{i}}$ and evaluation of Lense-Thirring precession timescales via $P_{\rm prec}=\frac{\pi}{3a_{*}}\frac{GM}{c^{3}}r^{3}_{sph}\left[\frac{1-(r_{in}/r_{sph})^{3}}{\ln(r_{sph}/r_{in})}\right]$.
papers.reason: The paper reports high-resolution VLBI observations of the microquasar GRS 1915+105 during its obscured phase, discovering a massive milliarcsecond-scale jet reorientation with offsets up to $57^{\circ}\pm 8^{\circ}$ and ruling out rapid Lense-Thirring precession in favor of a radiation-driven warped accretion disc.

papers.title: Jets and winds from the most powerful compact object in NGC 5408
papers.result: The compact radio counterpart is variable and unresolved (size $\lesssim 20\ {\rm pc}$), peaking at $L_{\rm 5.5\,GHz} \approx 7.6\times 10^{35}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$ with a steep spectrum $S_{\nu} \propto \nu^{-\alpha}$ ($\alpha \approx 1.1 \pm 0.1$). Optical continuum is fit by an inflated blackbody with $T_{\rm bb} \approx 4600\ {\rm K}$, $R_{\rm bb} \approx 1700\ R_\odot$, and $L_{\rm bol} \approx 4.4\times 10^{39}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$, which faded by $\sim 2\ {\rm mag}$ between 2010 and 2024. Broad optical emission lines decreased in flux by a factor of $\sim 50$ (broad ${\rm H}\alpha$ dropped to $F({\rm H}\alpha) = (23\pm 2)\times 10^{-16}\ {\rm erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$ with FWHM narrowing from $\approx 1700$ to $\approx 1100\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$). A diffuse hot plasma bubble ($kT \approx 0.9\ {\rm keV}$, radius $\approx 1''$) implies shock kinetic power $P_{\rm k} \approx 2\times 10^{40} f^{1/2}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$, while narrow ${\rm He\ II}\ \lambda 4686$ emission requires an ionizing luminosity $L_{\rm ion} \sim 10^{40}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$, hidden along the line of sight by Compton-thick obscuration.
papers.problem: Understanding the nature of an enigmatic compact source in NGC 5408 displaying extreme radio and optical luminosities, severe apparent X-ray faintness ($L_{\rm X} \lesssim 10^{38}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$), and an inflated cool optical photosphere exceeding stellar evolution limits.
papers.method: Multi-epoch analysis combining ATCA/VLA radio imaging and spectral index fitting ($S_\nu \propto \nu^{-\alpha}$), HST optical aperture/PSF photometry, VLT/FORS2 and VLT/MUSE integral field spectroscopy for nebular line diagnostics and outflow kinematics, and Chandra ACIS-S sub-pixel imaging and spectral fitting (`apec + power-law`). Wind envelope scale is modeled via $R_{\rm w} \approx (3/2)(\kappa \dot{M}) / (4\pi v_{\rm w})$.
papers.reason: The paper identifies and characterizes NGC 5408 X-2 as an extreme, Compton-thick super-critical accretor/microquasar exhibiting relativistic jets ($L_{\rm radio} \sim 7.6\times 10^{35}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$) and a massive optically thick outflow with kinetic jet bubble power $P_{\rm k} \sim 2\times 10^{40}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$. It directly informs studies of compact object relativistic jets, photoionized nebulae, and circumstellar wind interactions.

papers.title: XMM-Newton and NuSTAR quasi-simultaneous follow-up of the very high energy flare of PKS~1725+123 in August 2025
papers.result: The blazar's X-ray spectrum resolves into two distinct emission components: a soft component with photon index $\Gamma \gtrsim 2.5$ dominant at $E < 2\,\mathrm{keV}$ that fades within $\sim 14\,\mathrm{h}$, and a hard component with $\Gamma \sim 1.7-1.9$ dominant at $E > 2\,\mathrm{keV}$ that subsequently brightens by a factor of $\sim 1.5$. This traces the transition of the jet emission from a temporary intermediate-synchrotron-peaked (ISP) state back to a low-synchrotron-peaked (LSP) state, with intrinsic emission region size constrained to $R \le c t_{\rm intr} \sim 7 \times 10^{16} - 4 \times 10^{17}\,\mathrm{cm}$ assuming Doppler factors $\delta \approx \Gamma \sim 5.9-35$.
papers.problem: Disentangling the spectral transition across the broadband SED valley (between the synchrotron tail and the inverse-Compton rising edge) during a rare very high energy (VHE, $E > 100\,\mathrm{GeV}$) flare of the neutrino-associated blazar PKS 1725+123.
papers.method: Bayesian spectral fitting using BXA and UltraNest with W-stat on time-resolved spectra (GTIs of $\Delta t = 10\,\mathrm{ks}$ for XMM-Newton $0.2-12\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $\Delta t = 40\,\mathrm{ks}$ for NuSTAR $3-79\,\mathrm{keV}$) testing single- and double-power-law models (`TBabs*(zpowerlaw + zpowerlaw)`).
papers.reason: The paper presents quasi-simultaneous XMM-Newton and NuSTAR spectral-timing observations of the blazar/neutrino candidate PKS 1725+123 after its 2025 VHE flare, directly tracking the spectral evolution across the SED dip of a relativistic jet.

papers.title: SS 433 Eastern Jet Turbulence Revealed by Spatially-Resolved IXPE Data Analysis
papers.result: The eastern extended X-ray jet shows uniform electric vector position angles (EVPA $\sim 0^\circ$) perpendicular to the $\sim 94^\circ$ jet axis, establishing jet-aligned magnetic fields. The sheath exhibits suppressed polarization relative to the head and spine ($>3.2\sigma$ multi-zone improvement over single-zone), corresponding to enhanced turbulence $\tau = \delta B / B_0 \gtrsim 1.8$ compared to $\tau \lesssim 1.5$ in the spine and head (a factor of $\sim 2$ increase). For a photon index $\Gamma = 1.54$, the theoretical synchrotron maximum polarization is $\Pi_0 = \Gamma / (\Gamma + 2/3) \approx 69.8\%$, and the inferred post-shock flow yields an Alfvén Mach number $M_{\rm A} = 1300 \times (\frac{v}{0.08c}) (\frac{B}{12\,\mu\mathrm{G}})^2 (\frac{0.2\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}}{n_{\rm H}})^2 \gg 1$, proving magnetic tension cannot stabilize shear flows.
papers.problem: Resolving whether the reduced X-ray polarization in the SS 433 eastern jet boundary is caused by macroscopic magnetic field reversals or boundary-layer shear turbulence generated by jet-ambient interactions.
papers.method: Event-by-event unbinned maximum likelihood fitting in Stokes $q$-$u$ space using LeakageLib to eliminate Ricean bias, incorporating high-resolution Chandra spatial and spectral templates across 2–8 keV to segment the jet into head, spine, and sheath components, and modeling turbulence via $\tau = \delta B / B_0 = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}\frac{\Pi_0 - {\rm PD}}{{\rm PD}}} \sin i$.
papers.reason: This work uses spatially-resolved IXPE X-ray polarization modeling to measure magnetic turbulence in the SS 433 eastern jet, directly probing relativistic jet-medium shear interactions relevant to compact object high-energy outflows.

papers.title: Evidence for strong shocks in the ISM of small radio sources
papers.result: Small-scale radio sources ($10\,\mathrm{kpc} \le D \le 15\,\mathrm{kpc}$) exhibit significantly broader $[\mathrm{O\,III}]$ profiles (median $W80 = 694\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ vs $518\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ for large sources $D \ge 25\,\mathrm{kpc}$, with an extreme tail $W80 > 1300\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ exclusively in small sources), lower $[\mathrm{Ne\,V}]\,\lambda 3426$ detection rates ($30\%$ vs $58\%$ at $>3\sigma$), and systematic displacement toward LINER-like emission-line ratios, driven by jet kinetic power $Q \simeq 3\times 10^{38}\,f^{3/2}(L_{151}/10^{28}\,\mathrm{W\,Hz^{-1}\,sr^{-1}})^{6/7}\,\mathrm{W}$.
papers.problem: Distinguishing whether the perturbed kinematics and optical emission line ionization in compact radio galaxies are governed by radiative accretion-disk photoionization or by fast radiative shocks driven directly into the multiphase ISM by confined jets.
papers.method: Cross-matched VLASS with DESI DR1 ($0.15 < z < 0.5$) applying a cut $L_{\rm 3\,GHz} > 10^{24}\,\mathrm{W\,Hz^{-1}}$ to yield 44 small ($10\text{--}15\,\mathrm{kpc}$) and 33 large ($\ge 25\,\mathrm{kpc}$) sources; performed multi-Gaussian decomposition on optical emission lines to measure kinematic broadening $W80$, BPT line diagnostics ($[\mathrm{O\,I}]/\mathrm{H}\alpha$ vs $[\mathrm{O\,III}]/\mathrm{H}\beta$), and compared against jet kinetic power $Q$ scaling relations.
papers.reason: This study analyzes the interaction between compact relativistic jets and the ISM using DESI and VLASS data, establishing that small, confined jets drive strong radiative shocks that perturb gas kinematics and dominate ionization over photoionization.

papers.title: A Wolf-Rayet nebula in its disruption phase: high-resolution radio observations of PCG 11
papers.result: The nebula's integrated radio continuum exhibits a spectral index $\alpha = 0.03 \pm 0.03$ ($S_\nu \propto \nu^\alpha$), confirming dominance by optically thin thermal free-free emission with electron density $n_e \sim 2 \times 10^2\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$. The central star WR 75ab is detected for the first time in radio with $\alpha_\star = 0.9 \pm 0.35$ and an inferred mass-loss rate $\dot{M} \sim 1.7 \times 10^{-5}\ M_\odot\ \mathrm{yr^{-1}}$. Wind ram pressure at the inner boundary ($R_0 - a \simeq 0.6\ \mathrm{pc}$) is $P_{\rm w}/k \simeq 1.6 \times 10^7\ \mathrm{K\ cm^{-3}}$, exceeding the shell thermal pressure by a factor of 4--6, while the absorbed ionizing photon rate $Q_{\rm abs} \simeq 8 \times 10^{46}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$ is only $\sim 0.3\%$ of the stellar Lyman-continuum budget $Q_{\rm H} \sim 10^{49.4}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
papers.problem: Observing and resolving the transitional disruption phase of massive-star bubbles, where hydrodynamic instabilities break the swept-up circumstellar shell into porous structures while maintaining dynamical coupling to the central wind.
papers.method: Multi-frequency radio interferometry using MeerKAT (S-band at 2.6 and 3.1 GHz, and L-band at 1.28 GHz) combined with ATCA (5.5 and 9.0 GHz in 6 km and EW352 configurations), combined with 3D geometric forward-modeling comparing azimuthally averaged radial profiles of spherical shell, torus, and hollow cylinder geometries.
papers.reason: This work presents high-resolution MeerKAT and ATCA radio observations resolving the fragmented, porous circumstellar shell and detecting the central Wolf-Rayet star WR 75ab, constraining the mass loss and pre-supernova circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction environment.

papers.title: Quasi-normal Modes and Instabilities of Rotating Relativistic Stars
papers.result: For self-bound strange stars (MIT bag model, $M_0 = 1.57\,M_\odot$), the quadrupolar $f$-mode CFS instability neutral point ($\omega_{\mathrm{in}}=0$) is determined at rotational-to-gravitational potential energy ratio $\beta = T/|W| = 0.1023$, the Jacobi-like neutral point ($\omega_{\mathrm{ro}}=0$) at $\beta = 0.1665$, and the Krein collision (dynamical bar-mode instability threshold) at $\beta \simeq 0.2661$. For APR4 neutron stars ($M_0 = 2\,M_\odot$), the retrograde $f$-mode triggers CFS instability at dimensionless spin $\chi = J/M^2 = 0.5638$, while the $r$-mode scales as $\omega_{\mathrm{ro}}/\Omega \simeq 0.5238 + 0.4019\chi^2$ with radiation damping timescales scaling as $\tau_f^{-1} \simeq k_f M R_e^2 |\omega_{\mathrm{in}}|^5/\Delta$ and $\tau_r^{-1} \simeq k_r M R_e^4 \Omega^6$.
papers.problem: Accurately computing the non-axisymmetric and axisymmetric quasi-normal mode spectrum and determining the precise onset of secular and dynamical rotational instabilities in fully general relativistic, rapidly rotating stars without Cowling approximations.
papers.method: Formulation of a coupled fluid-spacetime quadratic eigenvalue problem $(\mathbf{K}_0 + \sigma\mathbf{K}_1 + \sigma^2\mathbf{K}_2)\mathbf{x} = 0$ derived from the second-order Einstein-fluid action in the Lorenz gauge ($Z_b = \nabla^a \tilde{h}_{ab} = 0$) using a spectral Ritz-Galerkin discretization, combined with exterior complex scaling ($r = r_b + s e^{\mathrm{i}\vartheta}$) to implement outgoing gravitational radiation boundary conditions.
papers.reason: The paper presents a comprehensive general relativistic formulation and Ritz-Galerkin spectral framework to compute quasi-normal modes and instability thresholds (such as the CFS and bar-mode instabilities) of rapidly rotating relativistic stars, directly relevant to newborn neutron star central engines and gravitational wave asteroseismology.

papers.title: Multimessenger astrophysics drives the case for an Australian Gravitational-Wave observatory
papers.result: In a CE+ET two-site network, the median probability of localizing down to a single host galaxy within $V_{90}$ is only $P=0.006$; adding an Australian station with A♮ or C♮ sensitivity increases this median probability to $P=0.05$ and $P=0.65$, respectively. Overall, a 3-detector network enables $24\%\text{--}61\%$ of injected kilonovae to identify a unique host galaxy purely from GW data, and achieves up to 8 multimessenger detections per year with median sky localizations reaching $1-10\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ (and down to $\sim 0.1\,\mathrm{deg}^2$).
papers.problem: Investigating how the lack of long southern-hemisphere baselines severely limits GW parameter estimation, causing large sky localization areas ($\Omega_{90}$) and 3D comoving volume uncertainties ($V_{90}$) that hinder optical/infrared kilonova follow-ups by Rubin (VRO) or Roman and impede unique host galaxy identification.
papers.method: Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) parameter estimation using TaylorF2 waveforms over $10\,\mathrm{Hz} \le f \le 1024\,\mathrm{Hz}$ ($f_{\mathrm{ISCO}} = [6^{3/2} 2\pi M_{\mathrm{tot}}]^{-1}$) requiring network signal-to-noise ratio $\rho_{\mathrm{net}} \ge 15$ and condition number $c = e_{\max} / e_{\min} \le 10^{15}$; coupled with Redback two-component kilonova modeling (gray opacities $\kappa_1=10\,\mathrm{cm^2\,g^{-1}}$, $\kappa_2=35\,\mathrm{cm^2\,g^{-1}}$, disk wind velocity $v_{\mathrm{ej},2}=0.05\,c$) and $90\%$ comoving volume calculation: $$V_{90} \simeq \frac{\Omega_{90}}{41253\,\mathrm{deg}^2}\,\frac{4\pi}{3}\,\frac{(d_L+\Delta d_L)^3-(d_L-\Delta d_L)^3}{(1+z)^3}$$.
papers.reason: This paper presents quantitative Fisher information matrix simulations demonstrating that adding an Australian gravitational-wave detector to 2G and 3G networks drastically shrinks sky localizations to $1-10\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ and enables robust kilonova/GRB multimessenger host galaxy identifications.

papers.title: Photon arrival time lags in 3D radiative transfer with SKIRT
papers.result: The code successfully recovers time lag distributions in arbitrary 3D geometries. In optically thick media, late-time transmission lags decay exponentially as $F_{\mathrm{t}}(t) \propto \exp(-\tau_{\mathrm{es}} c \,\delta t / D)$, with the mean time lag $\langle\delta t\rangle$ converging to the skin-depth lag $\delta t_{0.5} \equiv 2 d_{0.5}/c$. Owing to $\sigma_{\mathrm{PA}}(E) \propto E^{-3}$, neutral Fe K$\alpha$ fluorescence ($6.38\text{--}6.42\ \mathrm{keV}$, threshold $7.112\ \mathrm{keV}$) penetrates deeper and exhibits longer arrival delays than the continuum, producing a peak reverberation lag $\tau_{\mathrm{peak}} \approx 2.39 \times 10^6\ \mathrm{s}$ ($\approx 28\ \mathrm{d}$) for an AGN torus model around a $M_\bullet = 10^7 M_\odot$ black hole. Simulation efficiency is characterized by $\mathrm{FOM} \equiv 1 / (R^2 T)$ with convergence criteria $R < 0.1$ and $\mathrm{VOV} < 0.1$.
papers.problem: Self-consistently calculating energy-dependent photon arrival time lags, reverberation transfer functions, and Compton echo profiles across complex, non-spherical 3D circumstellar and circumnuclear media around high-energy compact objects.
papers.method: Implemented path-length accumulation in 3D Monte Carlo code SKIRT: photon packets track cumulative spatial path $\mathcal{D} \coloneqq \mathcal{D} + |\mathbf{r}_{i} - \mathbf{r}_{i-1}|$, with peel-off emission corrected for coordinate origin projection $\mathcal{D} \coloneqq -\mathbf{\hat{n}}_{\mathrm{obs}}\cdot\mathbf{r}_0$ and exit lag $\delta t = (\mathcal{D} - \mathbf{\hat{n}}_{\mathrm{obs}} \cdot \mathbf{r}_{i})/c$. Handled Klein-Nishina electron scattering and photoelectric absorption with Fe K$\alpha$ fluorescence, and convolved transfer functions with damped random walk (DRW) light curves to compute cross-correlation functions (CCF).
papers.reason: This work extends the open-source 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer code SKIRT to compute photon arrival time lags, providing a self-consistent tool for high-energy reverberation mapping and echo studies in complex compact object environments.

papers.title: Carbon-Reaction Constraints on Stellar Evolution: White-Dwarf Heating, Carbon-Burning Products, and Black-Hole Masses
papers.result: For accreting carbon-oxygen white dwarfs at $\dot{M} = 10^{-7}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the Bayesian median rate delays the thermal equilibrium $L_{\rm nuc} = L_{\nu} + L_{\gamma}$, yielding a central temperature $\sim 2.57\%$ higher and central density $18.9\%$ higher than standard CF88 rates. In $20\,M_{\odot}$ stars at core carbon exhaustion, the updated rates and branching increase ${}^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$ retained mass by $+10.78\%$ and decrease ${}^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ by $-28.70\%$. Across low metallicities ($Z = 10^{-5}$), constraining the astrophysical factor to $S_{\rm tot}(300\,\mathrm{keV}) = 118 \pm 17\,\mathrm{keV\,b}$ sets the maximum black-hole mass at the lower edge of the pair-instability gap to $61.48 \lesssim M_{\rm BH,max}/M_{\odot} \lesssim 77.35$, where $M_{\rm BH} \simeq M_{\rm initial} - M_{\rm wind} - M_{\rm PPISN} - \Delta M_{\rm collapse}$.
papers.problem: Uncertainties in the $^{12}\mathrm{C}+^{12}\mathrm{C}$ thermonuclear fusion rate, its proton-to-$\alpha$ branching ratio, and the $^{12}\mathrm{C}(\alpha,\gamma)^{16}\mathrm{O}$ cross section introduce major ambiguities in white dwarf ignition conditions, intermediate-mass isotope production, and the pair-instability supernova black hole mass gap.
papers.method: MESA stellar evolution simulations incorporating a Bayesian $^{12}\mathrm{C}+^{12}\mathrm{C}$ thermonuclear rate $R(T_{9}) \equiv N_{A}\langle\sigma v\rangle$, the temperature-dependent proton-to-$\alpha$ branching ratio $q(T_{9}) = R_p/R_\alpha$, and the specific carbon heating rate $\epsilon_{\rm C+C}(\rho,T) = \frac{\rho X_{\rm C}^{2}}{2A_{\rm C}^{2}} N_{A} R(T_{9}) Q_{\rm eff}$, integrated across white dwarf accretion rates $\dot{M} = (0.3\text{--}1.0) \times 10^{-7}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and helium star models with metallicity $Z=0.00142$ alongside scaled $Z=10^{-5}$ models.
papers.reason: This paper evaluates the impact of updated Bayesian carbon-fusion rates and carbon-helium rates on white-dwarf heating and the pair-instability black-hole mass boundary, providing crucial nuclear inputs for compact object formation and supernova progenitor modeling.

papers.title: Fermi-LAT Detection of Extended GeV Emission toward the Middle-aged Supernova Remnant G156.2+05.7
papers.result: Fermi-LAT confirms extended GeV emission with an extension $R_{68} = 0.84^{\circ} \pm 0.09^{\circ}$ ($\mathrm{TS}_{\mathrm{ext}} = 75.7$, $\Delta\mathrm{AIC} = -102.2$). Broadband SED modeling strongly favors a hybrid leptonic-hadronic scenario ($\Delta\mathrm{BIC} = 30.2$ over pure leptonic) with required proton energy budget $W_p(>1.22\,\mathrm{GeV}) \simeq 1.4\times 10^{50}\left(\frac{n}{1\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}}\right)^{-1}\left(\frac{d}{2.7\,\mathrm{kpc}}\right)^{2}\,\mathrm{erg}$ and conversion efficiency $\varepsilon_{\rm cr} \equiv W_p/E_{\rm SN} \simeq 0.14\left(\frac{n}{1\,\mathrm{cm^{-3}}}\right)^{-1}\left(\frac{d}{2.7\,\mathrm{kpc}}\right)^{2}$, ruling out single-zone tenuous ambient medium ($n=0.036\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}$) which would require $W_p \approx (3.7\text{--}4.0)\,E_{\rm SN}$.
papers.problem: Whether the gamma-ray emission in middle-aged SNR G156.2+05.7 originates from leptonic inverse Compton scattering or hadronic proton-proton collisions, and whether cosmic ray proton acceleration is energetically viable in its low-density ambient environment.
papers.method: Binned 2D likelihood morphological analysis and spectral fitting with Fermipy on 17 years of Fermi-LAT Pass 8 data (100 MeV–1 TeV), combined with ${}^{12}\mathrm{CO}$ survey data and MCMC broadband SED modeling using Naima with injected cutoff power-law particle spectra $\frac{dN}{dE} = N_0 \left(\frac{E}{E_0}\right)^{-\alpha} \exp\left(-\frac{E}{E_{\mathrm{cut}}}\right)$.
papers.reason: The paper detects extended GeV gamma-ray emission from the middle-aged supernova remnant G156.2+05.7 using 17 years of Fermi-LAT data and constrains cosmic ray acceleration and target densities via broadband leptonic-hadronic modeling.

papers.title: How Fast do Black Holes Spin?
papers.result: Using 2D GRMHD simulations across $\chi \in [0, 0.99]$, the equilibrium spin $\chi_{\rm eq}$ (where $\langle\dot{\chi}\rangle = 0$ for $\dot{\chi} = \dot{J}_h/M^2 - 2\chi\dot{M}_h/M$) is shown to depend sensitively on magnetic topology: a fiducial model ($\beta_{\max} = 100$) reaches $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.88$, multiple loops give $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.87$, strong magnetic fields ($\beta_{\max} = 10$) rapidly disrupt the torus shifting turnover to $\chi \in [0.37, 0.71]$, while radially modulated magnetic flux permits near-extremal spin $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.98$. The physical spin evolution rate scales as $\dot{\chi}^{\rm phys} \approx 2\times 10^{-8} f_{\rm Edd}\dot{\chi}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, implying evolution timescales $>10^{13}\,{\rm yr}$ for Sgr A* under its current low accretion rate.
